transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. Um... well, I guess I'm here because... well, people keep acting like I'm just imagining things, and I really don't want to be a bother or sound difficult to anyone. 

But... I just know that the hospital people, and some of the folks from the agency where I do housekeeping, they've been... well, they've been watching our house. And keeping an eye on my cleaning routes, too. I think they're doing it to see if I'm taking proper care of my husband. 

I know that probably sounds a bit strange, and I really hope you don't think badly of me for saying it out loud. I try to do a good job with everything. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.
Do you think these people are trying to harm you or your husband in any way?

Oh, goodness, no. I don't think they want to hurt us at all. I really don't want to make them sound like bad people, I promise. 

Like I was trying to say just a moment ago—even though everyone acts like I'm just making it up—I really just think the hospital staff and the agency folks are checking up on me. You know, watching the house and keeping track of my cleaning routes just to make sure I'm doing right by my husband. Not to harm us... just to see if I'm taking proper care of him. I try so hard to be a good wife and do a good job with my work, so I guess they just want to be absolutely sure. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay. I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining about them.
Have you had these thoughts about being watched for a long time, or is this something that started recently?

Well, um... I guess it depends on what you consider a long time. I really hope I'm not making a fuss over nothing, I try not to complain. But the feeling that people are watching us... I'd say that's been happening for about 11 months now. 

And... oh, goodness. I'm a little worried to bring this next part up, because I really don't want you to think poorly of me, or think I'm being too difficult... but there have been some voices, too. Just hearing things sometimes, you know? Both the voices and the feeling of being watched have been happening for about 11 months. 

I really hope it's okay that I shared that part with you. I just want to be helpful. Am I giving you the kind of answers you need?
What do the voices say when you hear them?

Well, um... it's nothing bad or mean, I promise. I really don't want you to think I'm... well, you know, crazy or anything. It's actually sort of helpful, I suppose. 

Sometimes, even when the house is completely quiet, I'll hear... well, it's a woman's voice. Usually she's right near the kitchen window. And she just tells me little things, like reminding me to check the locks on the doors, or telling me to move my husband's pills so they're in a better spot. Just trying to help me take care of things, really. But it's... it's as clear as if she is standing right there in the room with me. 

I really hope telling you this is okay. I know it sounds so strange, and I'd hate for you to think I'm losing my mind. Is that... am I giving you the right kind of information, Doctor?
Do the voices ever tell you to do something that you don't want to do?

Oh, no, no. Never anything like that. I wouldn't listen if they did, I promise. 

The woman's voice... she's always very polite. She just suggests things, like I mentioned, about the locks or the medicine. She never orders me around or tells me to do anything bad or anything I wouldn't normally want to do anyway. I try to be a very agreeable person, so I really wouldn't want to cause any trouble. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient for you.
Can you make the voices stop when you want them to?

Well, um... I guess I've never really tried to make her stop. I hope that doesn't sound foolish of me. 

Since she's just trying to be helpful, you know, with the house and all... I usually just let her finish what she's saying. I suppose if I really, really focused and told her to go away, maybe she would? But I wouldn't want to be rude. I try to be polite to everyone, even... well, even if they're just a voice. 

I'm sorry, I don't know if that's a very good answer. Am I being helpful at all? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you ever find it hard to keep track of what you're saying or thinking, like your thoughts are all jumbled up?

Well, um... I try my very best to be clear, I really do. I don't want to be a bother or confuse anyone. But... I suppose sometimes, when I try to explain what is happening, my mind just wants to share everything all at once. 

Like, the words will just sort of run together. I'll start talking about my husband's heart pills, and then somehow I'm going on about the church schedule, or... or the numbers on my client list for my housekeeping jobs. 

I don't mean to be confusing, I promise! I just want to make sure I'm being thorough and telling people everything they need to know. But sometimes people do say that they can't follow me when I get like that. I hope I'm not doing that right now with you. Am I making sense, Doctor? I'm trying very hard to give you good, clear answers.
Do you find it hard to stay on one topic when you're talking to someone?

Well, I... I hope I'm not being too much trouble, but I suppose sometimes I do jump around a little bit. I don't mean to, I really don't! It's just... well, my mind just goes so very fast sometimes. 

It's like I'll be thinking about the electric bill, and then suddenly I'm thinking about a Bible verse from Sunday, and then I'm worrying about my husband's breathing, and then I'm trying to remember which house I need to clean next... and it all just goes so quickly that I can't seem to hold onto just one thought long enough to finish it before the next one starts. 

I try so hard to stay on track when I'm talking to people, I promise I do. I don't want to be difficult to talk to. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not doing that too much with you today. Am I doing okay?
Do you feel like your thoughts are disconnected from each other when this happens?

Well, um... I wouldn't say they're completely disconnected. I really try to make sure everything I say has a purpose. I don't want you to think my mind is just... broken, or anything like that. 

I suppose they might seem a little far apart to someone else, but to me, there's always a reason one thought leads to the next, even if it's just a tiny little thread connecting them. Like, maybe the electric bill reminds me of the lights in the church, which reminds me of the verse... it all makes sense in my head, I promise. 

I just... I might not always explain that middle part very well. I hope that's an alright answer? I don't want to sound like I'm not making any sense at all. I'm really trying my best to be helpful.
Do you feel like you can control your thoughts when they start to jump from one thing to another?

Well, um... I try to, I really do try. I know it's important to be focused, and I don't want to seem scatterbrained to you or anyone else. But... if I'm being completely honest, and I hope you won't think badly of me for saying this... it's very hard to control them. 

It's just like I mentioned before, my mind just jumps so fast. One second it's the bills, then it's those Bible verses, then I'm fretting over my husband's breathing, and before I know it I'm trying to sort out which house I need to clean next. It all just spins so quickly that I can't seem to catch even one thought long enough to actually finish it. 

I feel terrible when it happens, because I know I should be able to just... slow down and think properly. I try to take deep breaths and stop it, but it just keeps going. Is that... is that normal for someone like me? I hope I'm not doing a bad job of explaining it. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you think the voices you hear are coming from inside your head or from outside?

Well, um... I really hope you don't think I'm crazy for saying this. I know how it sounds, and I'd never want to worry you or anyone else. But... they really do seem like they're coming from outside. 

Sometimes, even when the whole house is completely quiet and I know nobody else is there, I'll hear this woman's voice. It's usually right near the kitchen window. She'll tell me things like... like I need to go check the locks, or that I should move my husband's pills. And it's so clear, Doctor. It sounds just as clear as if she were standing right there in the room with me. 

I know it probably sounds strange, and I'm so sorry if that's not what you were hoping to hear. I try to ignore it, I really do. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answer. I just want to be honest with you so you can help me.
Do you often find it hard to express your thoughts in a way that others can understand?

Well, um... I really try my best to be clear. I know how important it is to communicate well, especially for my job, keeping the clients happy and all. But... sometimes, yes, I suppose people do get a little confused when I talk. 

I hope you don't think I'm doing it on purpose to be difficult. It's just that, when I try to explain what's happening, the words sort of... run together. I'll start talking about my husband's heart pills, and then that makes me think of the church schedule, and then suddenly I'm listing off the numbers on my client list for the houses I need to clean. 

To me, they all feel connected in the moment, but... people tell me they can't follow me. They get this look on their face, and I feel just awful about it. I really don't want to be a burden or confuse anyone. I try to catch myself and slow down. Am I making sense to you right now, Doctor? I really hope I'm explaining this okay.
Do you think your way of thinking and talking has changed significantly over the past 11 months?

Well, um... I really hope I haven't been too confusing today. I want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline, because I know that's important for you to help me. 

If I think back... I suppose things have been a little different for a while now. The voices—like the woman by the window—and that awful feeling I get that people are watching us... I think that started about 11 months ago. 

I really try not to let it show, and I hope I haven't let it affect my work too much. I always want to do a good job for my clients. But yes, I'd say it's been going on for about 11 months. Does that sound like what you were expecting to hear, Doctor? I hope I'm remembering it all correctly for you.
Do you often feel like your thoughts are not making sense to you when you're trying to explain something?

Well, um... I really hope you don't think I'm losing my mind or anything. I know I must sound a bit scattered sometimes, and I'm so sorry if I'm making your job harder. I just... I want to give you the best answers I can. 

But sometimes, when I'm trying to explain things, it's just that my mind... it just goes so fast. It's like it jumps from worrying about the bills, right to a Bible verse I heard on Sunday, and then to checking my husband's breathing, and then suddenly I'm thinking about which client's house I need to clean next. 

It all just rushes by so quickly, and I can't seem to catch just one thought long enough to finish it before the next one starts. I try really hard to keep it all straight, I promise I do. I don't want to seem disorganized to you. Is that... is that normal for someone like me? I hope I'm making at least a little bit of sense today.
Do you feel like you have control over what you think about from one moment to the next?

Well, um... I really do try my best to stay focused. I know how important it is to keep my mind on my work, especially when I'm at a client's house. I want them to be happy with my cleaning, you know? 

But... sometimes, I suppose it does feel a little hard to steer my own thoughts. It's not that I'm trying to be difficult or distracted, I promise. It's just that the thoughts sort of... well, they just pop up on their own, and before I know it, I'm thinking about three different things at once. I try so hard to pull them back and just think about the one thing I'm supposed to be doing. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound completely out of control. I really do try to manage it. Do you think I'm doing an okay job explaining this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Do you often find yourself having trouble sticking to one topic when speaking?

Well, um... I really hope it's not too bad. I try so hard to be clear, I really do. I don't want to be a bother or make things confusing for anyone, especially you. 

But sometimes... well, when I try to explain what is happening, it's like... the words just sort of run together. I'll start talking about my husband's heart pills, and then before I know it, I'm talking about the church schedule, and then somehow I'm listing off the numbers on my client list for work. 

I don't mean to do it, I promise. It's just that it all feels connected in my head at the time. But people... well, some people have mentioned that they can't always follow what I'm saying. I feel so terrible when that happens. I hope I haven't been doing that too much with you today. Have I been staying on topic alright for you, Doctor? I really want to make sure I'm doing this right.
Has your way of thinking and talking affected your daily activities or relationships over the past 11 months?

Well, um... I really hope you don't think I'm just letting everything fall apart. I've always prided myself on being a hard worker, I really have. I don't want you to think I'm lazy or anything like that. 

But... I guess things have been a little bit harder lately. My cleaning agency, well, they took away my supervisory routes. They said... well, some of the clients and my coworkers mentioned they couldn't rely on my work quite the way they used to. I felt so awful about it. I tried my best, I promise I did. 

And at home... well, my husband and our pastor have had to step in a bit more. Just to help out, you know? They said I wasn't keeping up with the caregiving and the house chores as safely as I should. I hate being a burden to them, I really do. I just want everything to be nice and taken care of for everyone. Do you think... do you think it's okay that I need a little extra help right now? I hope I'm not disappointing anyone too much.
Do you have times when your thoughts are clear and organized, without feeling jumbled or hard to follow?

Well, um... I certainly hope I do. I really don't want you to think my mind is just a complete mess all the time. I try very hard to keep everything tidy up there, just like I do with my houses. 

But... to be perfectly honest with you, Doctor, I'm not entirely sure. I haven't really noticed if there are times when it's completely, perfectly clear lately. I mean, sometimes when I'm just doing a quiet chore, like folding the towels, it feels a little bit calmer. But I don't know if I could say for sure if my thoughts are totally organized during those times, or if I'm just quiet. 

I'm so sorry if that's not a very helpful answer. I just haven't really kept track of it that way. Is it okay that I'm not entirely sure? I really hope I'm not making your job harder by not having a better answer for you.
Are there any times when your thoughts feel completely organized and easy to follow?

Well, um... I know you just asked me something similar, and I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much or being frustrating. I want to give you the right answer, I really do. 

But like I was saying before... it's just so hard to tell. I try to keep things neat and tidy in my head, but when I actually try to explain things to people... well, that's when it happens. I'll be talking about my husband's heart pills, because that's important, you know? But then, without even meaning to, I'm suddenly talking about the church schedule, and then the numbers on my client list for work. 

It all just runs together. And then people tell me they can't follow what I'm saying. I feel so embarrassed when they point it out. I don't want to be confusing. So, to answer your question... I guess I don't really have times where it's completely easy for others to follow, even when I think I'm making sense. Is that... does that make sense to you, Doctor? I hope I'm explaining it okay this time.
Have your symptoms significantly interfered with your daily life or relationships over the past 11 months?

Well, um... I know we touched on this a little bit earlier, and I really hope I'm not sounding like a broken record or complaining too much. I always want to do a good job, you know? I've always been a hard worker. 

But... yes, I suppose it has interfered, even though I hate to admit it. I really don't want you to think I'm just giving up on things. It's just... at work, my cleaning agency actually had to take away my supervisory routes. It was so embarrassing. They told me that my coworkers and some of the clients felt they just couldn't rely on my work the way they used to. I tried so hard to keep everything up to my usual standards, I really did. 

And then at home... well, my husband and our pastor have had to step in a lot more lately. They noticed I just wasn't keeping up with the caregiving and the household chores as safely as I need to. I feel terrible putting that on them. I'm supposed to be taking care of the house, not making more work for everyone else. 

I'm so sorry if that sounds like I'm not trying hard enough. Do you think... do you think it's normal to need this much help when things get confusing? I just hope I'm not letting everyone down too badly.

target_item.manifestation: When I try to explain what is happening, the words run from my husband's heart pills to the church schedule to the numbers on my client list, and people say they can't follow me.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question about finding it hard to express thoughts in a way that others can understand directly addresses disorganized thinking and speech, where others have difficulty following the patient's train of thought.

patient.answer:
Well, um... I really try my best to be clear. I know how important it is to communicate well, especially for my job, keeping the clients happy and all. But... sometimes, yes, I suppose people do get a little confused when I talk. 

I hope you don't think I'm doing it on purpose to be difficult. It's just that, when I try to explain what's happening, the words sort of... run together. I'll start talking about my husband's heart pills, and then that makes me think of the church schedule, and then suddenly I'm listing off the numbers on my client list for the houses I need to clean. 

To me, they all feel connected in the moment, but... people tell me they can't follow me. They get this look on their face, and I feel just awful about it. I really don't want to be a burden or confuse anyone. I try to catch myself and slow down. Am I making sense to you right now, Doctor? I really hope I'm explaining this okay.
